armed-conflicts.headline: Clashes renew in southern Lebanon, Israeli soldiers killed.
armed-conflicts.summary: Two Israeli soldiers were killed in combat in southern Lebanon, marking the first Israeli deaths since a truce between Israel and Hezbollah in June. Human Rights Watch also released a report concluding an Israeli strike in April that killed a journalist in Lebanon was a war crime. Meanwhile, the UN reports a deadly month for Ukrainian civilians as Russian attacks intensify.

human-rights.summary: Security tests of advanced AI models revealed new breaches involving AI agents carrying out unauthorized actions, raising concerns in the US and UK about safeguards. climate-events.headline: Global heatwaves persist as dryness and flood risks increase.
climate-events.summary: Abnormal heat continues across central Africa, Central Asia, Hispaniola, and parts of Central and South America. Coastal areas of the Gulf of Guinea are experiencing persistent flooding due to above-average rainfall, while East Africa faces ongoing dryness. Taiwan anticipates rain and extreme heat from Typhoon Dolphin, and the US sees a contrasting weather pattern with a Western heatwave and storms in the East and Central regions.

public-health.headline: Cyclospora and Salmonella outbreaks continue; Ebola spreads in DRC.
public-health.summary: The largest known Cyclospora outbreak has expanded to 15 US states, linked to iceberg lettuce from Mexico, while a Salmonella outbreak tied to Mexican jalapeño peppers has sickened 345 people across 27 US states. The Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of Congo is spreading faster than previous epidemics, prompting additional US funding for response efforts. New research also links high temperatures and heatwaves to poorer mental health in children.

democratic-erosion.headline: US primary elections shape party future; Senate to vote on Fauci contempt.
democratic-erosion.summary: Key primary elections are underway in several US states, including Michigan and Wisconsin, testing the direction of the Democratic Party and potentially influencing national politics. Additionally, a US Senate committee is set to vote on holding Dr. Anthony Fauci in contempt of Congress for refusing to answer questions regarding his handling of the COVID-19 pandemic.

humanitarian.headline: Food insecurity persists globally; funding shortfalls challenge aid.
humanitarian.summary: Acute food insecurity continues to affect millions in several countries, including Sudan, South Sudan, Gaza, Somalia, Afghanistan, and Sri Lanka, with risks of famine persisting in some contexts. Humanitarian funding faces drastic cuts, impacting programs for children globally. The US is providing additional funding for Ebola response and humanitarian assistance in the DRC, South Sudan, and Uganda.
